profile.headline: Scientific Software Developer - NOAA Contractor
profile.summary:
I am a theoretical physicist with emphasis in computational condensed matter physics, and I am passionate about physics fundamental research and programming. I have also found joy in teaching and creating physics educational material for higher education. 

I currently work at Gama-1 Technologies as a contractor in a Software Developer and Integrator position. In this position I work in conjunction with the U.S. "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration" (NOAA) in the ASSISTT team, that provides development, curation, cloud integration, deployment, and software testing services for scientific software applications using the "SAFe Agile" framework.

I am co-author of several peer reviewed publications, in high-impact physics/chemistry journals. For this work I received the Research Excellence Award at Iowa State University in May 2017.  I have other articles in preparation.

My strengths are in computer programming and mathematical modeling of complex systems such as those found in applied chemical physics. Specifically, my Ph.D. research focused on developing analytic models for reaction-diffusion processes based on data gathered from kinetic Monte Carlo simulations and Langevin molecular dynamics simulations. Through this research, I developed, implemented, and integrated computer programs using programming languages such as Fortran 90, C++, Java, Python and Mathematica. In the process, I developed several interactive visualization tools that enabled me to visualize and analyze data in an efficient and interactive way, integrating the above-mentioned programming languages. I also have experience with C# and the Microsoft Office Suite.

In addition to the broad range of skills acquired through my Ph.D. experience, I have also gained experience working in multidisciplinary teams. My research projects often involved researchers whose expertise were in chemistry, physics, materials engineering, mathematics, or other areas of science and engineering. As such, I frequently collaborated with experts from other disciplines and communicated research findings to a broad audience. This experience led me to expand my knowledge and learn effective communication skills in team settings.

I spend my leisure time with my wife and my daughter, and occasionally playing a round of golf in the local course.

positions.title: Research Associate
positions.description:
My main research focus is in stochastic processes in complex systems. The specific project consists in using Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to obtain an analytic theory to determine the concentration profile, and thus product yield, of a simple stereo-selective irreversible conversion reaction. The goal of the research is to create a framework to model more complex systems, in both geometry and interactions, using high-performance computers and computing (HPC). The current status of the project is on-going.

I am also actively collaborating with Dr. Alejandro Travesset-Casas, professor in the Department of Physics at Iowa State University, in assessing the thermodynamics stability of perovskite nanocrystals using the molecular dynamics Python-based software package HOOMD-blue. I am projected to start working as a volunteer in January 2020.

Instructor of record in charge of designing and delivering the lecture material, creating the evaluation material and grading. Actively participated in Departmental level decisions and advising students on career decisions.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching and Research Assistant
positions.description:
As a graduate research assistant my main research was focused in stochastic processes in complex systems. The specific project consisted in using Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to obtain an analytic theory to determine the concentration profile, and thus product yield, of a simple stereo-selective irreversible conversion reaction. This theoretical model was implemented to validate experimental results from the esterification reaction in functionalized mesoporous silica of 4-nitrobenzaldehy to 4-(4-nitrophenyl)-2-butanone. For these projects, I wrote, implemented and integrated several computer programs in C++, Python, Fortran 90 and Wolfram Mathematica to gather, analyze, visualize and publish the data in high-impact journals. These projects resulted in six peer-reviewed publications and a research excellence award in May 2017.

As a graduate teaching assistant, I was responsible for delivering the recitation material and laboratory instruction for the introductory physics courses. During the Fall 2015 semester I was a mentor in the First Year Graduate Student Mentorship initiative. This initiative consisted in mentoring incoming first year graduate students into the graduate student life in the graduate physics program in Iowa State University, by discussing and advising students on social and academic issues they were having.

use in 2023 fire-season air quality models.
